extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and responding to Office actions during patent examination, especially requirements for examinations, rejections, citations of prior art, and form/contents of Office actions. Targets examiner procedures and applicant submission practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up an application for examination ... the examiner shall make a thorough study thereof and shall make a thorough investigation of the available prior art relating to the subject matter of the claimed invention. The examination shall be complete with respect both to compliance of the application or patent under reexamination with the applicable statutes and rules and to the patentability of the invention as claimed, as well as with respect to matters of form, unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination must cover statutory compliance, patentability, and matters of form. International-type search requirements (see separate rubric) may apply. Use available search resources to locate best references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and explanation in Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant, or in the case of a reexamination proceeding, both the patent owner and the requester, will be notified of the examiner’s action. The reasons for any adverse action or any objection or requirement will be stated in an Office action and such information or references will be given as may be useful in aiding the applicant ... to judge the propriety of continuing the prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State reasons for adverse actions/objections and include useful information/references to enable applicant to evaluate whether to continue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-type search availability
rubrics_metrics.description: An international-type search will be made in all national applications filed on and after June 1, 1978. Any national application may also have an international-type search report prepared thereon at the time of the national examination on the merits, upon specific written request therefor and payment of the international-type search report fee set forth in § 1.21(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must note when international-type searches apply; applicants may request and pay for such reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of examiner's action (limited exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s action will be complete as to all matters, except that in appropriate circumstances, such as misjoinder of invention, fundamental defects in the application, and the like, the action of the examiner may be limited to such matters before further action is made. However, matters of form need not be raised by the examiner until a claim is found allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit scope of action only for specified circumstances (misjoinder, fundamental defects). Do not require raising form objections until claim allowability stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection – general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is not considered patentable, or not considered patentable as claimed, the claims, or those considered unpatentable will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify which claims are rejected and on what basis (novelty, obviousness, statutory bars, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite best references and designate pertinent parts
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command. When a reference is complex or shows or describes inventions other than that claimed by the applicant, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select strongest/principal references and, where relevant, identify pages/sheets/figures relied upon; explain pertinence if not apparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of pertinence and specificity for rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The pertinence of each reference, if not apparent, must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevance isn't obvious, provide an explanation linking reference disclosure to claim limitations; specify which claims are affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on admissions and examiner knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant ... as to any matter affecting patentability and, insofar as rejections in applications are concerned, may also rely upon facts within his or her knowledge pursuant to paragraph (d)(2) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admit reliance on applicant statements where appropriate. When relying on facts within personal knowledge, follow affidavit/support procedures (see separate rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/(f)/(g) prior art under 103
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter which is developed by another person which qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 against a claimed invention unless the entire rights to the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned by the same person or organization or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person or organization at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check ownership/assignment status before using 102(e)/(f)/(g) art in 103 rejections; document basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclusion by statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims in any original application naming an inventor will be rejected as being precluded by a waiver in a published statutory invention registration naming that inventor if the same subject matter is claimed ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a published statutory invention registration exists naming an inventor, determine whether it precludes claims in the application or reissue and reject if so; cite specifics of the preclusion criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation data requirements (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: If domestic patents are cited by the examiner, their numbers and dates, and the names of the patentees will be stated. If domestic patent application publications are cited ... the publication number, publication date, and the names of the applicants will be stated. If foreign published applications or patents are cited, their nationality or country, numbers and dates, and the names of the patentees will be stated, and such other data will be furnished as may be necessary to enable the applicant ... to identify the published applications or patents cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient bibliographic data so applicant/patent owner can identify and retrieve each cited reference; include page/sheet details when only part is relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee personal-knowledge rejections require specificity and affidavit
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rejection in an application is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an employee of the Office, the data shall be as specific as possible, and the reference must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee, and such affidavit shall be subject to contradiction or explanation by the affidavits of the applicant and other persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to supply employee affidavit support for factual rejections based on personal knowledge; ensure specificity to withstand challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance must be recordable and commentable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes that the record of the prosecution as a whole does not make clear his or her reasons for allowing a claim or claims, the examiner may set forth such reasoning. The reasons shall be incorporated into an Office action rejecting other claims ... or be the subject of a separate communication to the applicant or patent owner. The applicant or patent owner may file a statement commenting on the reasons for allowance within such time as may be specified by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document reasons for allowance on the record; allow opportunity for applicant comment; failure to respond does not imply anything.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action content and attachments (PTOL-326, PTO-892, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the current first action procedure, the examiner signifies on the Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 certain information including the period set for reply, any attachments, and a 'Summary of Action' ... The list of references cited appears on a separate form, Notice of References Cited, PTO-892 ... The attachments have the same paper number and are to be considered as part of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTOL-326 and PTO-892 as required; ensure attachments are properly paginated and treated as part of the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply paper identification recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to Office actions should include the application number as well as the 4-digit art unit number and the examiner’s name to expedite handling within the Office. Further, applicants are encouraged to include the 4-digit confirmation number on every paper filed in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage applicants to include these identifiers to speed processing; examiners should reference them in actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: For 103 rejections explain combination/modification reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: For rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103, the way in which a reference is modified or plural references are combined should be set out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly explain the rationale for combining or modifying references to make the claimed invention obvious; map claim limitations to reference teachings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special treatment for pro se/informal cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In exceptional cases, as to satisfy the requirements under 37 CFR 1.104(c)(2), and in pro se cases where the inventor is unfamiliar with patent law and practice, a more complete explanation may be needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide more detailed explanations and guidance in Office actions where the applicant is pro se or unfamiliar with procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisor responsibilities for persistent/old applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The supervisory patent examiners are expected to personally check on the pendency of every application which is up for the third or subsequent official action with a view to finally concluding its prosecution. Any application that has been pending five years should be carefully studied ... and every effort made to terminate its prosecution. The application is to be considered 'special' by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPEs should monitor third-or-more actions and 5-year pendency to ensure timely resolution and, if appropriate, prioritize termination of prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite appropriate prior art nearest to claimed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: During the examination of an application or reexamination of a patent, the examiner should cite appropriate prior art which is nearest to the subject matter defined in the claims. When such prior art is cited, its pertinence should be explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on closest prior art; explain why it is relevant to the claims; consider applicant-cited art and information disclosure statements (MPEP § 609).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term and priority-date search considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should search all applications based on the actual U.S. filing date of the application rather than on the filing date of any parent U.S. application for which priority under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c) is claimed. Examiners should cite of interest all material prior art having an effective filing date after the filing date of the U.S. parent application but before the actual filing date of the application being examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of 20-year term measured from earliest claimed priority and adjust searches to reflect actual filing dates; cite intervening-material prior art as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed applications should generally include citations for printing
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed applications should generally contain a citation of pertinent prior art for printing in the patent, even if no claim presented during the prosecution was considered unpatentable over such prior art. Only in those instances where a proper search has not revealed any prior art relevant to the claimed invention is it appropriate to send an application to issue with no art cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a set of pertinent prior art citations is prepared for the patent as issued; use parent application citations for continuations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of cited references — automatic furnishing and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of cited references (except as noted below) are automatically furnished without charge to applicant together with the Office action in which they are cited. Copies of the cited references are also placed in the application file for use by the examiner during the prosecution. Exceptions: copies of references cited by applicant in accordance with MPEP § 609, § 707.05(b), and § 708.02 are not furnished with the Office action; copies of references cited in continuation applications if previously cited in the parent application are not furnished; other listed exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and furnish copies of examiner-cited references with Office actions except where enumerated exceptions apply. Use PTO-892 and file-wrapper procedures to manage copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for providing copies of references
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist in providing copies of references, the examiner should: (A) Write the citation of the references on form PTO-892, 'Notice of References Cited'; (B) Place the form PTO-892 in the front of the file wrapper; (C) Include in the application file wrapper all of the references cited by the examiner ... (D) Make two copies of each reference which is to be supplied and which has been located in a place other than the classified search file ... identify one copy as 'File Copy' and the other copy as 'Applicant’s Copy'. (E) Turn the application in to the technical support staff for counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these steps to ensure applicant and file receive copies; identify copies in red ink; ensure technical support receives complete set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design application citation/copy exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of design applications, procedures are the same as set forth in MPEP § 707.05 (a)-(g) except that less than the entire disclosure of a cited U.S. utility patent may be supplied with the action by the Design Group. Copies of all sheets of drawings relied on and of the first page of the specification are furnished without charge. Any other subject matter, including additional pages of specification relied on by the examiner will be provided without charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For design apps, at minimum provide cited drawing sheets and first page of spec; provide additional material when relied upon; applicants may order full patents via copy services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-submitted citations and related information
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP § 609 sets forth positive guidelines for applicants, their attorneys and agents who desire to submit prior art for consideration ... Submitted citations will not in any way diminish the obligation of examiners to conduct independent prior art searches, or relieve examiners of citing pertinent prior art of which they may be aware, whether or not such art is cited by the applicant. Prior art submitted by applicant in the manner provided in MPEP § 609 will not be supplied with an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant submissions do not replace examiner searches; applicant-submitted citations are generally not furnished back with the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of listing and notation of pertinent features
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing references for the first time, the identifying data of the citation should be placed on form PTO-892. No distinction is to be made between references on which a claim is rejected and those formerly referred to as 'pertinent.' With the exception of applicant submitted citations ... it is recommended that the pertinent features of references which are not used as a basis for rejection be pointed out briefly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTO-892 for first-time citations; briefly note pertinent features of references not used for rejection to assist applicant and public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic/data details required for different reference types
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. patent application publications: publication number, publication date, names of the applicants, class, and subclass. U.S. patents: patent number, patent date, name of the patentee, class and subclass. Foreign patents: patent number, kind code, citation date, name of the country, name of the patentee, and U.S. class and subclass if appropriate; IPC subclass/group/subgroup where applicable. Where less than the entire disclosure of the reference is relied upon, the sheet and page numbers specifically relied upon and the total number of sheets of drawing and pages of specification must be included. For publications, author, title, date, pages or plates, and place of publication, or place where a copy can be found, will be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the specified bibliographic elements depending on reference type; include page/sheet indicators when partial reliance; encourage inclusion of kind codes on U.S. docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication citation conventions and minimal data rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of books and periodicals SHOULD NOT be such as abbreviated because an abbreviation ... will not be sufficient to identify the publication. References are to be cited so that anyone reading a patent may identify and retrieve the publications cited. Bibliographic information provided must be at least enough to identify the publication: author, title, and date. For periodicals, at least the title of the periodical, the volume number, date, and pages should be given. These minimal citations may be made ONLY IF the complete bibliographic details are unknown or unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid abbreviations; provide full bibliographic details whenever possible. Use minimal info only as last resort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic document identification
rubrics_metrics.description: An electronic document is one that can be retrieved from an online source (e.g., the Internet, online database, etc.) or sources found on electronic storage media (e.g., CD-ROM, magnetic disk or tape, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing electronic documents, ensure sufficient retrieval information (URL, database identifier, date accessed, or document ID) so the document can be located; treat electronic references per the same identification standards as other publications.
